results.question: Which department has the highest average salary?
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id ORDER BY avg_salary DESC LIMIT 1
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY d.id HAVING AVG(p.base_salary) = (SELECT MAX(avg_salary) FROM (SELECT AVG(p.base_salary) AS avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY d.id)) LIMIT 100

results.question: List the top 3 highest paid employees

results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(p.base_salary + p.bonus) AS total_salary FROM employees e JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY e.id ORDER BY total_salary DESC LIMIT 3

results.question: Which employees have never been absent?
results.expected_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM attendance_logs WHERE status = 'Absent')
results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN attendance_logs a ON e.id = a.employee_id WHERE a.status != 'Absent' OR a.status IS NULL GROUP BY e.id HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN a.status = 'Absent' THEN 1 END) = 0 LIMIT 100

results.question: What is the total payroll cost per department?

results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name, SUM(p.base_salary + p.bonus) FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY d.id LIMIT 100

results.question: Which project has the most employees assigned to it?
results.expected_sql: SELECT p.project_name, COUNT(ep.employee_id) as employee_count FROM projects p JOIN employee_projects ep ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY employee_count DESC LIMIT 1
results.generated_sql: SELECT p.project_name, COUNT(ep.employee_id) FROM projects p JOIN employee_projects ep ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.id HAVING COUNT(ep.employee_id) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT project_id, COUNT(employee_id) AS cnt FROM employee_projects GROUP BY project_id) AS sub) LIMIT 100

results.question: Show departments where the average salary is above 6000
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 6000
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY d.id HAVING AVG(p.base_salary) > 6000 LIMIT 100

results.question: List employees who have both Present and Absent attendance records
results.expected_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN attendance_logs a ON e.id = a.employee_id WHERE a.status IN ('Present', 'Absent') GROUP BY e.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.status) = 2
results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN attendance_logs al ON e.id = al.employee_id GROUP BY e.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT al.status) > 1 AND COUNT(CASE WHEN al.status = 'Present' THEN 1 END) > 0 AND COUNT(CASE WHEN al.status = 'Absent' THEN 1 END) > 0 LIMIT 100

results.question: Rank employees by salary within each department
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, department_id, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) as rank FROM employees
results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name, e.department_id, p.base_salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY p.base_salary DESC) as salary_rank FROM employees e JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id ORDER BY e.department_id, salary_rank LIMIT 100

results.question: Show the running total of payroll by month
results.expected_sql: SELECT month_year, base_salary + bonus as total, SUM(base_salary + bonus) OVER (ORDER BY month_year) as running_total FROM payroll
results.generated_sql: SELECT month_year, SUM(base_salary + bonus) AS total_payroll FROM payroll GROUP BY month_year ORDER BY month_year LIMIT 100

results.question: Find the highest paid employee in each department using a subquery
results.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, e.salary, e.department_id FROM employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department_id = e.department_id)
results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name, e.department_id, p.base_salary FROM employees e JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id WHERE (e.department_id, p.base_salary) IN ( SELECT e.department_id, MAX(p.base_salary) FROM employees e JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY e.department_id ) LIMIT 100

results.question: Show department budgets compared to their total employee salaries using a CTE
results.expected_sql: WITH dept_salary AS (SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) as total_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department_id) SELECT d.name, d.budget, ds.total_salary FROM departments d JOIN dept_salary ds ON d.id = ds.department_id
results.generated_sql: WITH department_budgets AS ( SELECT d.id, d.name, SUM(p.budget) AS total_budget FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN employee_projects ep ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ), department_salaries AS ( SELECT d.id, d.name, SUM(p.base_salary) AS total_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ) SELECT db.name, db.total_budget, ds.total_salary FROM department_budgets db JOIN department_salaries ds ON db.id = ds.id LIMIT 100
